title: Daypart deploy rotation and observability checkpoints
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for a daypart-aware deployment rotation and observability checkpoint rhythm. Aim: reduce blast radius during high-variance traffic windows, make handoffs explicit, and ensure telemetry gating is clear for low-latency, high-priority releases.

Context / Motivation:
- We still see occasional latency spikes after late-afternoon rollouts when traffic shifts across geos.
- Traditional single-window releases (midnight / early morning) aren't always possible for product-driven timelines.
- We need a repeatable micro-ops cadence so smaller teams can ship safely across multiple "dayparts" (morning, midday, evening, overnight).

High-level approach:
1) Partition day into 4 dayparts: morning (06:00-11:59), midday (12:00-15:59), evening (16:00-21:59), night (22:00-05:59).
2) Assign a deployment rotation slot per team per week; teams get one non-night slot and a single night slot per month.
3) Each deployment must pass the Observability Checkpoints (see below) before traffic ramp.
4) Canary ramping uses traffic-slice gating: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with hold times and telemetry acceptance criteria.

Quick decision rules (notes-to-self):
- If any critical error rate increases > 0.2% absolute in a 5-minute window at any ramp step, immediately rollback to prev variant and alert SRE.
- If p95 latency degrades > 15% for a service critical path (model routing, auth), pause rollout and call the on-call.
- Night slots: restrict to emergency or pre-approved infra-only changes unless explicitly signed off by product.

Preflight checklist (to be completed 48h -> 2h before slot):
- 48h: Feature flags defined, rollout plan written and linked (PR + feature-flag key).
- 24h: Capacity test run — basic smoke with synthetic traffic matching expected sequence lengths. Attach CSV: latency/CU usage.
- 12h: Telemetry threshold plan posted to the release thread (Slack + Confluence link).
- 2h: Final smoke in staging, confirm no new errors, attach smoke logs.
- 30m: Brief handoff: deploy owner posts kickoff message, on-call acknowledges.

Observability Checkpoints (must pass during each hold):
- Metrics to watch (top-line): request_rate, error_rate (4xx/5xx), model_inference_latency_p50/p95/p99, kv_cache_hit_rate, token_cost_per_k, throughput_tokens_per_sec.
- Traces: sample traces for any increased tail latency. Link to trace sampler dashboard.
- Logs: check recent 30m for noisy exceptions (model OOMs, kernel failures).
- Alerts that must be green: model-routing-backends, batcher-saturation, disk-pressure, network-ebs-errors.
- Acceptance criteria (example): during 10-minute hold -> 5m rolling windows: error_rate <= baseline + 0.15% and p95 latency <= baseline + 12%.

Canary ramp timings (recommended):
- Step 0 (deploy): 0% traffic, CI & smoke pass.
- Step 1 (0.5%): 15 min hold.
- Step 2 (2%): 30 min hold.
- Step 3 (10%): 45 min hold and deeper inspection (traces + embedding/response quality sample).
- Step 4 (50%): 60 min hold; run synthetic parity job to compare token cost and quality by sample prompts.
- Step 5 (100%): finalize, tag release, notify stakeholders.

Rollout calendar (example week):
- Monday morning: Team A slot (non-night).
- Tuesday midday: Team B slot (non-night).
- Wednesday evening: Team C slot (non-night).
- Thursday night: Reserved night slot (infra-only unless exception).
- Friday morning: Buffer/rescue slot (small fixes / rollbacks).
- Notes: Reserve one rolling buffer per week for emergency patches.

On-call & handoff script (short):
- Deploy owner posts "deploy kickoff" in #deployments with links: PR, feature-flag, rollout plan, canary slices.
- On-call acknowledges and sets a temporary incident channel if any metric hits gating threshold.
- At each hold: deploy owner posts "hold-check" with 1-line metric snapshot and decision (continue/hold/rollback).
- Finalize: owner posts final release note + release tag and closes the thread.

Rollback matrix (fast):
- Immediate soft rollback: flip feature flag -> 0% traffic (fastest, no infra change).
- Revert deploy (if feature flag not available): revert to previous image and redeploy -> follow standard rollback window and postmortem.
- If downstream degradation persists after rollback (unlikely but possible): scale down new frontends and open incident.

Release notes - draft (to be included in the release thread and release notes doc):
- Short title: feature/infra name + team + daypart slot (e.g., "model-autotune-v2 — infra — Wed-evening").
- Summary: 2–3 lines: what shipped, why, and expected user impact.
- Ops notes: canary slices, special config toggles, KVS migrations, any DB migrations and backwards-compatible notes.
- Known limitations: quick bullet list.
- Rollback procedure: one-line reference to the rollback matrix above.

Example release-note draft (placeholder):
- Title: "kv-cache-indexing-fix — infra — Tue-midday"
- Summary: "Fixes a race during KV-index refresh that could cause degraded cache hit rate under sustained cold-start traffic. No schema changes. Expected: improved cache-hit in first 30s of new sessions; no user-facing behavior change."
- Ops: Canary ramping per standard daypart table. Watch kv_cache_hit_rate dashboard and kernel OOM alert.
- Known issues: should not be used in night slots until after 48h of production observation.

Telemetry samples & quality checks:
- Attach a 50-sample prompt set for semantic parity checks when model changes or quantization profiles change. Run nightly eval for 72h post-release for non-night releases.
- Flag any >1% drop in rank-based eval metrics to product & applied-ml.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to auto-assign daypart slots across teams when multiple PRs target same window? (current idea: first-come-first-claimed in the deployment calendar + conflict resolution via rotations lead).
- Metric baselines: need weekly baseline job to capture working medians for p95 and error rate per service. Who will own? (suggest: telemetry-team).
- Slack automation: can we add a bot to inject the 5m rolling snapshot at each hold? (ENG-2143 created).

Appendix: quick links + references:
- Feature-flag playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Feature+Flags
- Release calendar (prototype): https://sheets.redwood.ai/d/RELEASE-CALENDAR-2026
- Incident escalation notes: ENG-ONCALL-RUNBOOK

Notes-to-self / collaboration notes (rough):
- Evan: please validate the baseline scripts and add to ENG-telemetry job queue.
- Marta: can you prototype the Slack hold-checker for the 0.5% -> 2% step (lightweight webhook)?
- Kenji: confirm night-slot exception criteria and sign-off flow.

End of draft. This doc is intentionally procedural, not final — feel free to edit sections inline and mark terms as TODO where appropriate.
